title: Johnny Richards as a writer
summary: They sort out what Richards contributed and Handy calls him a marvelous but different writer.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Johnny Richards, now that I think of it, was responsible for some of
that stuff on that record, that first date. I think he did "Love Tales", didn't he?
"Love Tales" wasn't on that date. The album that Pollack made? It wasn't on there.
I don't think there was anything of Johnny's on there.
Now if Jack McKenney were here, he would be able to reel off all the dates and all the tunes.

I'll bet; sure he could. I'm not saying that Johnny was not as good a writer as I am; no way am I implying that. Johnny was a marvelous writer. He didn't have my sight; his sight was different. He looked in other directions than me. We were different writers.

That I don't know, because I didn't hear anything that he wrote from that point on.
He wrote some things for the Kenton band really to cry over, for that big 1952 band.
I'll send you some tapes of that band.
